messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: routing_policy_monitor detected a surge of cross-tier routes for tenant=greenpine at 2026-02-18T21:16:41Z — 512K reqs routed to hosted instead of dedicated for capacity_tier=gold. Potential tenant isolation lapse. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:

jessica (oncall): I'm on it. seeing errors in the routing service metrics, +50% requests flagged as 'fallback-hosted' from the dedicated pool around 21:12Z. Is there an active rollout?

sam (sre): Not from infra side. No deploys in last hour according to deploy-bot. logs show: `route_eval: policy_id=policy-09f3 eval_time=0.8ms action=fallback target=hosted reason=capacity_threshold` repeated.

jessica (oncall): Paging @tariq for routing policy/ML config — the fallback logic might be mis-evaluating tenant tags.

tariq (ml-routing): I'm here. pulling the last policy revision. this looks like the canary that was merged this morning to change region fallback ordering. grabbing policy blob...

--- policy excerpt ---
```yaml
policy_id: policy-09f3
match:
  - tenant.tag: gold
actions:
  - type: prefer_pool
    pool: dedicated_gold_v2
  - type: fallback
    order: [regional, hosted]   # expected order
```
--- end ---


tariq (ml-routing): wait — the compiled policy in production has `order: [hosted, regional]` for this policy. looks like the compile step inverted the order for policies with `prefer_pool` + `fallback`. that's why requests went to hosted first.

elena (platform): how did that slip through? CI should've caught mismatched compile output. can we revert the compiled artifact?

sam (sre): We can hotpatch routing evaluation to short-circuit fallback to hosted for `capacity_tier=gold` tenants. I can push a temporary rule to block hosted fallback while we fix compile. Doing `redwoodctl routing patch --id policy-09f3 --set 'fallback.block_hosted=true'` now.

deploy-bot: command accepted. patch queued, applying to 6 routing workers in eu-west-1, us-east-1.

sam (sre): Patch applied on 6 workers. Confirming metrics... hosted routes for greenpine down from 52% -> 2% over 40s. latency to dedicated pool normalizing.

jessica (oncall): Good. Maria, do we have customer-impact? any CS escalations?

maria (cs): Maria here — greenpine reported increased 5xxs around 21:13Z, about ~8 minutes of elevated errors for end-users; they saw timeouts and a few bad completions. I've opened a ticket and DM'd the account manager. They asked for a short incident summary.

jessica (oncall): Noted. We'll draft and share.

tariq (ml-routing): Root cause: compiler for routing policy (router-compiler v2.4.0) had a regression when `prefer_pool` + `fallback` existed together. unit tests missed the ordering edge-case. I'll revert the compiler to v2.3.7 and recompile policies.

elena (platform): Please recompile then push new artifacts. Also add a circuit-breaker: if more than 1% of tier-gold requests go to hosted in 60s, auto-block hosted.

tariq (ml-routing): On it. `router-compiler revert --to v2.3.7 && router-compiler compile --all --out /artifacts/policies/1767777` -> compile success.

deploy-bot: new compiled artifacts uploaded. rolling upgrade to router-eval workers in progress (6 nodes).

sam (sre): Rolling restart completed. Verified policy order now `regional -> hosted`. Sampling logs: `route_eval: policy_id=policy-09f3 action=prefer_pool target=dedicated_gold_v2` and later `no fallback to hosted` for greenpine.

jessica (oncall): Metrics look stable. greenpine traffic back to dedicated. I'll keep monitoring for next 30m. Maria, draft a customer note: what to include?

maria (cs): I'll include timeline, impact, and mitigation. request to confirm whether any data was exposed — looks like only routing to hosted changed compute location but payloads were encrypted in transit and logs show no retention beyond normal. I'll note that in the note and mention we enforced tenant isolation and deployed fix.

jessica (oncall): Good. Follow-up actions: 1) tariq to add unit tests for compile ordering, 2) elena to add runtime guard, 3) sam to run a canary that stresses routing decisions, 4) create incident postmortem doc and assign owner. Who volunteers to lead PM?

tariq (ml-routing): I'll own the postmortem writeup for routing side.

elena (platform): I'll own runtime guard PR.

sam (sre): I'll run the high-load canary and include verification steps.

jessica (oncall): Ok. Handoff: my shift ends in 20m. @alex (oncall-next) — I'll brief you in 15. No open mitigations; patch in prod, rolling completed, monitoring green.

alex (oncall-next): ack. I'll take watch. Add me to the postmortem thread.

jessica (oncall): incident closed (mitigated). tagging for postmortem: OWNER=tariq, SEVERITY=sev2, CUSTOMER=greenpine, DURATION=~8m elevated errors.

maria (cs): Customer notified with summary and we offered a call if they want details.

tariq (ml-routing): follow-up TODOs added to routing backlog: add unit test, add compile-time assertion, audit last 24h for any other inverted policies.

elena (platform): I'll open a PR for the circuit-breaker rule and add an observability alert when hosted-fallback share > 1% for any gold tenant.

sam (sre): I'll schedule the canary for tomorrow 02:00 UTC.

jessica (oncall): thanks all. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
